# Installation guide

Cabby supports Python 3.11 and 3.12. The commands below use Python 3.12.
The MISP fork's distribution name is `misp-cabby`. Python code imports
`cabby`, and the command-line tools use their existing `taxii-*` names.
Installing Cabby also installs `misp-libtaxii` (1.1.120 or later) for
TAXII 1.0 and 1.1 XML messages. The fork provides the `libtaxii` Python
module. See [MISP/libtaxii](https://github.com/MISP/libtaxii).

## Install uv

On macOS or Linux, run Astral's installer in a terminal:

```sh
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, run the installer in PowerShell:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Open a new terminal and check the installation:

```sh
uv --version
```

See the [uv installation guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
for package-manager alternatives. uv can download Python 3.12 automatically
when a command requests it.

## Install the TAXII command-line tools

Install the MISP fork from PyPI into an isolated tool environment.

```sh
uv tool install --python 3.12 misp-cabby
taxii-discovery --help
```

If your shell cannot find the command, run `uv tool update-shell` and open
a new terminal. Use `taxii-21 --help` for the TAXII 2.1 command (see [TAXII 2.1 guide](taxii21.qmd)). The installation also provides `taxii-collections`,
`taxii-poll`, `taxii-proxy`, `taxii-push` and `taxii-subscription`.

## Use Cabby in a Python project

From a uv project with a compatible Python requirement (for example,
`requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"`), add the MISP fork and verify the import:

```sh
uv add misp-cabby
uv run python -c "from cabby import create_client; print(create_client.__name__)"
```

uv records the dependency in `pyproject.toml` and the resolved version
in `uv.lock`.

## Install with pip

With a Python 3.11 or 3.12 virtual environment active, run
`python -m pip install misp-cabby`.

## Switch from the original distribution

Both distributions provide the same `cabby` module and CLI commands. In a uv
project that depends on `cabby`, run `uv remove cabby` before `uv add misp-cabby`.
For a pip installation, run `python -m pip uninstall cabby` before installing
`misp-cabby`. For a uv tool installation, run `uv tool uninstall cabby` first.

If your environment already contains the upstream `libtaxii` distribution,
install Cabby in a fresh environment. Both libtaxii distributions own the
same Python module and CLI files.

## Install directly from GitHub

To run Cabby's development version with dependencies from PyPI, use
`uv tool install --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/MISP/cabby.git` for the
CLI, or `uv add "misp-cabby @ git+https://github.com/MISP/cabby.git"` in a uv
project. For an editable checkout, see [Contributing and developing](developer.qmd).

To try a Cabby checkout before its required libtaxii version is on PyPI,
install the CLI from the checkout and give uv the matching MISP/libtaxii
revision. This example uses the merged source for `misp-libtaxii` 1.1.120.

```sh
uv tool install --python 3.12 \
  --with "misp-libtaxii @ git+https://github.com/MISP/libtaxii.git@1c4bfa13731eb22c8fd6b674c2f5f0d48be72820" .
taxii-discovery --help
```

## Versioning

Cabby uses `major.minor.revision` version numbers. The revision number identifies bug-fix releases.
